mission_01: Congratulations! You've mastered PCA basics, the cornerstone of dimensionality reduction. By standardizing data and applying PCA, you reduced correlated features to uncorrelated principal components while preserving maximum variance. You learned to interpret explained_variance_ratio_ to understand how much information each component retains. This skill is fundamental for data visualization, noise reduction, and preprocessing for machine learning models.
mission_02: Congratulations! You've learned t-SNE for high-dimensional data visualization. By applying t-SNE to the iris dataset, you created a 2D embedding that reveals cluster structure. t-SNE's ability to preserve local neighborhoods makes it ideal for visualizing clusters in high-dimensional data. You now understand that t-SNE is stochastic and requires careful parameter tuning for optimal results.
mission_03: Congratulations! You've explored UMAP, a modern dimensionality reduction technique. UMAP combines the cluster-preserving qualities of t-SNE with better global structure preservation and faster computation. You learned that UMAP is a versatile tool for both visualization and preprocessing, scaling well to large datasets that would be impractical for t-SNE.
mission_04: Congratulations! You've mastered variance-based feature selection. By using VarianceThreshold, you learned to identify and remove features that provide little discriminatory power. This simple, unsupervised method is an effective first step in any feature selection pipeline. You now understand that low-variance features are unlikely to contribute meaningfully to model predictions.
mission_05: Congratulations! You've learned Linear Discriminant Analysis for supervised dimensionality reduction. Unlike PCA, LDA uses class labels to find directions that maximize class separability. You discovered that LDA produces at most n_classes - 1 components and is particularly effective when class separation is the primary goal. This technique bridges dimensionality reduction and classification.
mission_06: Congratulations! You've mastered PCA component analysis. By examining explained variance ratios, cumulative variance, and component loadings, you developed a deep understanding of how PCA transforms data. You learned to determine the optimal number of components for a desired variance threshold, a critical skill for balancing dimensionality reduction with information preservation.
mission_07: Congratulations! You've learned Recursive Feature Elimination, a powerful wrapper-based feature selection method. By recursively removing the least important features based on model performance, RFE identifies optimal feature subsets. You now understand the trade-off between computational cost and selection quality, and you can interpret RFE's support_ and ranking_ attributes.
mission_08: Congratulations! You've compared three major dimensionality reduction techniques side by side. By applying PCA, t-SNE, and UMAP to the same data, you developed intuition for their complementary strengths: PCA for speed and global variance, t-SNE for cluster visualization, and UMAP for balanced performance. This comparative understanding enables you to select the right technique for any use case.
mission_09: Congratulations! You've mastered mutual information feature selection. By using SelectKBest with mutual_info_classif, you selected features based on their statistical dependency with the target, capturing both linear and non-linear relationships. This filter method is fast, model-agnostic, and effective as a first-pass feature selection technique.
mission_10: Congratulations! You've built a complete dimensionality reduction pipeline combining standardization, feature selection, and PCA. By chaining these techniques and evaluating model performance on reduced features, you demonstrated mastery of the full dimensionality reduction workflow. This pipeline approach balances computational efficiency with model performance, a critical skill for production machine learning systems.
